tc-elf.description: bare-metal m68k-elf binutils 2.42 + GCC 13.3.0 (C only, --with-cpu=68000), built from GNU release tarballs

tc-vbcc.description: vbcc 0.9g (m68k and 16-bit-int m68ks backends) + m68k-atari target 2019-10-04 + unix config; vasm/vlink from tc-gnu

tc-a68k.description: A68K 2.71 (Charlie Gibbs, 1991, public domain) built from its C source (Aminet dev/asm/A68kGibbs.lha); vlink from tc-gnu

tc-mint.description: the pinned sidecartridge/atarist-toolkit-docker Dockerfile as-is (m68k-atari-mint GCC 4.6.4 / binutils 2.30 from the vriviere PPA). Its upstream inputs (PPA packages, vasm/vlink/agtools 'latest') are NOT pinned by the candidate: versions are recorded from the built image, reproducibility is observed, not guaranteed

candidates.rationale: Every original-68000 target (192, 256, 128 KB cartridge, Amiga 256 KB ROM) builds with m68k-atari-mint GCC 4.6.4; 68030/68040/ColdFire/Vampire machine targets are excluded. The base-68000 images still contain runtime-guarded 68010+/68030/68040 instruction spans (CPU/MMU/cache detection in bios/processor.S, bios/68040_pmmu.S, bios/startup.S, util/bootram.S) that T002 must type as CPU-variant regions, never label as base-68000 code. The build stamps the current date into the image header, so the recipes pin the date seen by the build (XPLAT_DATE) to make the image digests reproducible on any day. The cpu_variant_source_files count is a tree-wide mnemonic heuristic, not evidence: it includes the ColdFire-only file and misses hand-encoded (dc.w) instructions.
candidates.label_evidence: compiler assembly (-save-temps) + assembler listings + emutos.map link map (T002)
candidates.lineage_hypothesis: one firmware lineage (EmuTOS project); the four targets are configurations, not independent programs

candidates.rationale: The authentic toolchain (course cc68x compiler and gen assembler) is not publicly reproducible. Under declared substitutes every C and assembly module compiles (vbcc 0.9g +tos16, vasm), but no executable links: a header defines initialised globals in every unit (psg.h) and the program relies on the cc68x runtime's gemdos binding. Object-level evidence only; not a historical rebuild.
candidates.label_evidence: vbcc emitted assembly + vasm listings at object level (T002)
candidates.lineage_hypothesis: one student-game lineage (two authors), C + assembly
prerequisites: cc68x / gen toolchain and its TOS runtime library (not publicly distributed)

candidates.rationale: pacman.s requires AmigaOS assembler includes (exec/, dos/, graphics/, intuition/, hardware/ *.i), lvo/*.i library-offset includes from the author's private include tree (amiga39_JFF_OS) and WHDLoad developer includes (whdload.i, whdmacros.i), none in the repository. Sprites/sounds are generated by the author's bitplanelib Python tools from ripped arcade graphics. No licence is declared and the bundled graphics are arcade rips: licensing review is also required. Provenance: by the author's own description this is a 1:1 port of the commercial arcade game by the author family of the galaga/xevious/mpatrol transcodes (not yet inspected for transcoded code); it is treated as commercial-derived and can never become clean truth through supplying the missing includes alone.

candidates.rationale: A library, not a program: no authored executable target. With the toolchain declared by its ST makefile (vbcc 0.9g, 16-bit int) and an environment-only case-insensitive header shim, 120 C modules compile. 7 fail on Windows backslash include paths. The assembly modules use Pure C PASM directives (export/import) that vasm rejects, and two use FPU instructions. No licence declared.
candidates.label_evidence: vbcc emitted assembly at object level (T002)
candidates.lineage_hypothesis: Reservoir Gods library lineage; would contaminate any program built on it

candidates.rationale: A line-by-line 68k transcode of the commercial arcade Z80 program, with graphics extracted from the arcade ROMs committed as C data, so the code derives from commercial code. Technically the core transcoded modules assemble with GNU as (-m68000, register-prefix-optional); the Amiga main module needs generated sound/graphics includes, and vbr.68k is deliberately 68010+. No licence declared. No licence decision can admit it: as commercial-derived code it is excluded from clean truth by provenance; the class records only that its own repository licence is also unresolved.
candidates.label_evidence: GNU as listings (if admitted after review)
